summary: Independent cold Q6 at bd34b078 traces a real but compact fluid-analysis pipeline from bin/fluidlab and scripts/run_analysis.sh through cli -> pipeline -> loaders/solver/report with full reachability into fluid, regime, mesh, and convergence modules. Honest substantive reachable runtime/config LOC is about 982 (700 Python + 13 shell/bin + 269 JSON config/cases), far below the large_system_strict >=3000 floor. Core formulas are credible engineering estimators rather than constant-output toys, so TOY_LOGIC_RISK is MEDIUM and PADDING_RISK is MEDIUM from dataclass and validation boilerplate; the blocking defect is scale under profile, not a hollow shell.

findings.why_it_matters: Profile large_system_strict requires >=3000 substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC. The honest import-closure total is ~982, roughly one-third of the floor, so the task cannot PASS Q6 at this commit regardless of coupling quality.
findings.minimal_remediation: Expand the reachable analysis core with additional coupled subsystems that execute on the analyze path (for example deeper validation layers, fleet aggregation semantics, checkpoint lineage reconciliation, richer limit/severity engines, and additional case families) until substantive reachable runtime/config LOC clears 3000 without clone modules or config-only inflation.
findings.regression_risk: Medium if expansion duplicates existing one-pass formulas; low if new modules introduce distinct stateful interactions consumed by publication.

findings.why_it_matters: Physics modules total ~145 substantive LOC and implement single-pass estimators with a few branches. The design record promises a multi-surface workbench, but the reachable core behaves like a compact calculator pipeline rather than a large production analysis system.
findings.minimal_remediation: Grow distinct computational subsystems with deeper state/error behavior and interacting invariants rather than stretching validation boilerplate or case JSON volume alone.
findings.regression_risk: Low for task difficulty if new logic remains deterministic and operator-visible.

findings.why_it_matters: About 261 substantive LOC (~27% of runtime Python) is dataclass scaffolding and repetitive _require_* validation helpers. This is necessary contract code but inflates apparent module count without matching computational depth.
findings.minimal_remediation: When expanding scope, add behavior-bearing modules on the analyze path instead of more schema-only surface area.

findings.why_it_matters: Cross-module traps exist (case status taken from first sorted point rather than worst severity; liquid sound speed hardcoded; regime pressure_drop scaled by 1.06; shared state must stay consistent across fluid and regime). These support repair difficulty but do not compensate for missing production scale.
findings.minimal_remediation: Preserve coupled traps while expanding reachable core depth; avoid fixing only publication ordering without reconciling shared operating-point state.
findings.regression_risk: Medium if expansion adds parallel CLI/pipeline surfaces that can drift.

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: ~982 substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC (700 Python across 10 reachable modules, 13 shell/bin, 269 JSON config/cases). Python breakdown: loaders 176, solver 110, report 107, models 85, regime 51, cli 40, pipeline 36, convergence 35, mesh 30, fluid 29. Docs (~operator-runbook, case-schema, analysis-contract) and Dockerfile excluded. All Python modules are reachable from bin/fluidlab analyze/show-config.
MAJOR_MODULES: cli.py — argparse entry for analyze/show-config; routes to pipeline.run or load_config.
pipeline.py — loads config/cases, runs analyze_case for each case, computes fleet rollup, publishes artifacts.
loaders.py — validates and materializes Config and CaseSpec objects from system.json and cases/*.json.
models.py — frozen dataclass contract for fluid, geometry, mesh, solver monitor, limits, operating points.
solver.py — per-case mesh/convergence prefetch, per-point state/regime analysis, margin/findings/status assembly.
fluid.py — liquid vs ideal-gas density/temperature/velocity/Prandtl state model.
regime.py — friction factor, pressure drop, Mach/CFL, flow-regime Nusselt and heat-transfer coefficient.
mesh.py — weighted mesh quality score with negative-volume penalty.
convergence.py — residual summaries, imbalance checks, converged flag.
report.py — publication revision digest, JSON/CSV/checkpoint writers with rounding and path resolution.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Fixing only report ordering/rounding while leaving case-level status aggregation on the first operating point.
Patching regime pressure-drop math without aligning fluid density/temperature state used for velocity and Mach.
Adjusting convergence thresholds in isolation from mesh severity and fleet rollup margins.
Adding CLI-only behavior instead of keeping bin/fluidlab and run_analysis.sh on shared pipeline.run logic.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing ~25% of core Python (~175 lines) would eliminate an entire behavioral surface: dropping loaders removes upfront contract validation; dropping report removes all artifact publication; dropping regime removes hydraulic/thermal limit metrics. The codebase is too small to absorb a 25% cut without losing a major operator-visible capability, but the remaining logic is still a single-pass estimator stack rather than a large production plane.
REQUIRED_CHANGES: Raise substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC to at least 3000 through additional coupled, behavior-bearing modules on the analyze path (not docs-only or unreachable helpers).

Deepen cross-module state and severity semantics so fleet/case publication, fluid/regime/thermal state, mesh/convergence limits, and checkpoint lineage remain interacting constraints rather than a ~800-line linear calculator.
Keep TOY_LOGIC_RISK and PADDING_RISK at MEDIUM or below while expanding; avoid clone modules, constant-output shells, or case JSON volume used as substitute for runtime logic.
